title: Retain dependent rows when their principal can be missing
goal: Use unconstrained relationships when reads must retain orphaned dependents, and distinguish that query decision from migration-only constraint omission.

selectionNotes: EF11 IsConstrained(false) omits the database foreign key and uses a LEFT JOIN for the required navigation. ExcludeForeignKeyFromMigrations only omits enforcement: the required navigation still uses INNER JOIN and drops an orphan. Both retain the model relationship and its index. The SQL2025 fixture inserts one matched and one orphan crate, then checks generated DDL, actual sys.foreign_keys/sys.indexes and executed results. The Required control deliberately removes its generated constraint solely to demonstrate the bad assumption. EF10 keeps a valid explicit GroupJoin/DefaultIfEmpty left join and explicitly omits the generated constraint; it cannot call IsConstrained. The schema script edit is bounded to this authored fixture, not a general migration rewriter. For production use reviewed migrations. No database referential-integrity guarantee remains: the application and data owner must handle absent principals and decide validation, repair and delete policy. Required CLR navigation annotations do not prevent null projections from an unconstrained join. SQL Server only; no Cosmos or other-provider parity.
